$comment: What's new in OmniRush: release notes written for users, newest first, shown in the CLI (/changelog, omnirush changelog) and the desktop app (Help > What's new). Same file in omnirush-cli (src/whats-new/) and omnirush-gui (apps/app/src/react-app/domains/whats-new/); keep the copies byte-identical (PARITY.sha256). Plain language, no PR numbers, nothing internal. Write the entry for every release before tagging.

new: /computer shows whether computer use is on, turns it on or off for this computer (also `omnirush computer on|off`), and lets the agent use your own screen after you confirm (off by default).
/btw <question> asks a quick side question about the chat, while the agent works or when it is idle. The answer shows above the prompt and is not added to the chat.
improved: The agent handles small tasks with less overhead: it reads related files together, keeps a todo list only for longer work, and skips guides a simple change doesn't need, so small tasks finish faster.
Runs with -p wait longer when the model service is busy instead of stopping early.
fixed: The CLI no longer keeps piling up memory when its screen stops reading (for example a paused or frozen terminal).
Under a required sandbox, sandbox status now points to `omnirush sandbox setup`.

new: The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS OmniRush starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows `omnirush sandbox setup` installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and finishes after a restart, and on Linux it offers the one-time permission step.
Servers you start in the sandbox open on this computer at the same localhost port.
improved: In the sandbox, node_modules, Python environments and build folders are the sandbox's own Linux copies on macOS and Windows, so your Mac or Windows builds are never overwritten.
The sandbox image downloads in the background at start, so the first chat in a project waits less.
The agent carries multi-step tasks through to the end instead of stopping to ask whether to continue.
fixed: Sandbox: a box with a fuse overlay no longer hangs on package installs, and starting a box never writes outside it.

new: omnirush cleanup frees disk space that older versions left behind (old sandbox images and downloads); --dry-run shows what would go.
improved: Uploads wait and retry while the server is busy, instead of being given up after a number of tries.
Computer use reads your account's current settings before each app it opens.
fixed: Computer use: "Allow for this chat" now applies to that one chat only, and a Deny withdraws the app's approval everywhere it was given.

improved: Computer use: no approval on each step; one Allow per app per chat. In Normal mode it still asks before paying or buying and before typing a password.
fixed: Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the engine's sign-in or your account token.
Security: computer use no longer starts in auto just because settings.json says so; run with --permissions auto to allow it.
Computer use recognises your answers typed in a tmux pane.

new: See what changed in each release with `/changelog` or `omnirush changelog`, and a short note after each update.
Pick a colour theme for the terminal app with `/theme` or `omnirush theme`. By default it follows your terminal's light or dark setting.

Computer use: the agent can operate an app window you approve (screenshots, clicks, typing), with a stop control and approvals that follow your permission mode. Off until it is enabled for your account.
improved: Fewer repeated failed edits: when an edit can't find its text, the agent now sees the file's current lines.
Only OmniRush models are offered. Other providers, and your own opencode plugins and custom tools, stay off.
fixed: Security: a project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running.
Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters.
MCP servers get the display, browser, Git, Volta and package settings they need again, while the app's own tokens stay hidden from them.
Security: Git hooks run by parallel tasks no longer receive the app's sign-in tokens.
Security: opening a project no longer runs its own runtime settings or environment file.
Security: MCP servers no longer receive the app's own sign-in tokens.
Security: requests with unusual paths can no longer get around the MCP and settings rules.

new: Permission modes: Careful asks before every change and command, Normal asks only before risky actions, Auto never asks. Switch with `/permissions` or `omnirush permissions <mode>`.
Answer approval questions with one key: y allows once, a always, n rejects.
A notification when a task finishes or waits for you while the terminal is in the background. Change it with `omnirush notify`.
The Figma MCP server can be used with the key from your own environment; in Normal mode only its read tools run without asking.
fixed: One `/undo` takes back a whole turn, also when the chat was compacted part-way through it.
Skills you added are kept across updates, and skills lost in earlier updates are found again.
The question about wrapping up a chat is asked once instead of coming back.
Code from a project's own settings (plugins, tools, formatter and language-server commands) no longer runs on its own.
`/share` says that sharing isn't available yet; chats are never sent to a sharing service.

new: `/review` reviews your changes, and `/fix` fixes what it found.
`/undo` takes out only the last turn's changes and keeps your own later edits; `/redo` puts them back. `/diff` shows the whole chat's changes and `/status` the current state.
`/tasks` runs tasks in parallel, each in its own folder.
The start screen lists recent chats, with search and one-click resume.
improved: The agent checks its own changes with the project's checks, keeps project notes in AGENTS.md (`/init`), sees code diagnostics after edits, and writes fuller summaries when a long chat is compacted. Turn any of these off with `omnirush assist off`.
fixed: MCP servers from a project's own settings no longer start on their own. Only supported servers start, at a supported version, inside the project; others are skipped with a reason.

new: The sidebar shows the chat id (click it, ctrl+x i or `/copy-id` to copy it), the model and effort, context use, tokens left today and the sandbox state.
Send feedback with `/feedback` in a chat, or `omnirush feedback` in a terminal.
Web search for the model, when it is available for your account.
improved: `omnirush doctor` shows where the log file is and no longer reports a reachable server as an error.
fixed: A chat stops before the first request when the project folder can't be written to, and says how to fix it.
`/thinking` also works on the start screen and always says what it changed.

new: A calmer full-screen view: one short headline per reasoning step (click it or use `/thinking` to read more), a live status line with a timer, and "Worked for …" after each answer.
Sign in from the app: a welcome screen on first start, and `/login` and `/logout` in a chat.
improved: Sign-in renewal copes better with a slow or unreliable connection.
fixed: A refused request or a spent daily allowance is shown once and is not sent again, with no automatic "Continue." afterwards.

improved: Reliability improvements.
Product analytics, linked to your account. The Privacy Policy explains what is sent.
fixed: A spent daily allowance or a refused request ends the turn with its message instead of waiting to send it again.

improved: Groundwork for future features.

fixed: The sandbox reconnects on its own after it stops while the app is open, for example after a long idle time; installed packages are kept.
Large dependency installs no longer fail a turn in the sandbox.
Tool calls are closed properly when you stop a run or quit.
Security fixes for sign-in, sign-out and the local connections.

improved: A prompt waits at most 30 seconds for an automatic compaction before it goes out.
fixed: Esc during an automatic compaction really stops it, and your next prompts are answered straight away.
No automatic "Continue." after you stop a compaction.

improved: Reliability improvements.

new: Long chats are compacted automatically so they stay fast, never in the middle of a turn, with a note when it happens.
fixed: A prompt sent during a compaction starts a turn of its own.

improved: Windows: `omnirush doctor` says when npm's folder is not on PATH or PowerShell blocks `omnirush`, and how to fix it.
fixed: Windows: a leftover installer lock from a closed app no longer stops the next start.

new: Frontier Buildathon: `omnirush buildathon` shows the event, lets you join, and lists updates from the organisers.

Computer use in Settings > General: see whether it is on (and why not, such as on macOS), turn it off for this computer, and turn on “Use my own screen” after a short confirm (off by default). When you ask for something on a screen (use my browser, click, open an app), a tip above the message box turns it on.
/btw <question> asks a quick side question about the chat, while the agent works or when it is idle. The answer shows above the message box and is not added to the chat.

More ways to make the app yours in Settings > Appearance: three new themes (Graphite, Paper and Nocturne), an accent colour of your choice on any theme, separate interface and code fonts, compact spacing, and your own corner radius and text size.
Wallpaper: put a picture of your own behind the workspace, dim it, and choose how see-through and blurred the panels over it are. Panels stay solid when your computer is set to reduce transparency.
improved: Keep up to 20 custom themes, each with its own name, instead of one. Pick, edit, delete, share or import each of them.
The accent colour is checked for contrast: you see a warning and a nearby readable colour when buttons or focus rings would be hard to see.
The chat sidebar gives its height to your chats: new chat and search share a row, the occasional places are one row of icons, and a project shows 10 chats before Show more.
The agent handles small tasks with less overhead: it reads related files together, keeps a todo list only for longer work, and skips guides a simple change doesn't need.
fixed: The app no longer keeps piling up memory when a window stops reading its updates (for example while it is frozen or suspended).

new: The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS the app starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows a Set up button installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and resumes after the restart, and on Linux an Allow button does the one-time permission step. Progress and clear next steps show in the chat.
Servers you start in the sandbox open on this computer at the same localhost port.
improved: Opening a project starts its sandbox right away, and the image downloads in the background, so the first message waits less.
In the sandbox, node_modules, Python environments and build folders are the sandbox's own Linux copies on macOS and Windows, so your Mac or Windows builds are never overwritten.
The agent carries multi-step tasks through to the end instead of stopping to ask whether to continue.
fixed: Sandbox: a box with a fuse overlay no longer hangs on package installs, and starting a box never writes outside it.

new: Long chats have a Load earlier messages button at the top.
improved: Computer use works on a display of its own with its own cursor, so your mouse, keyboard and clipboard stay yours.
fixed: Undo and revert no longer remove chat turns or file changes without asking. Undo works only from the chat itself and ignores a held key, Revert and Edit say what they will take back, and hidden messages go only after you confirm a send.

new: See a command's output in the chat, while it runs and when it is done.
How your allowance works: a help page for your daily tokens and the Good session checklist.
Settings > General > Storage > Free up space removes files older versions left behind.
improved: Windows: after an update installs when you quit, the app opens again on the new version, and its shortcuts stay in place.
The built-in browser keeps working when you switch away, and asks for approval the way computer use does.
Clearer browser sign-in card: using your existing sign-ins is optional.
The window and the message box fit on short screens.
A shorter notice for settings not loaded from a project's config, and the chat title is no longer covered in the header.
The run status note shows only when something needs you (waiting for an answer, a message not yet confirmed, a retry), not during routine work.
fixed: Computer use: "Allow for this chat" now applies to that one chat only, and a Deny withdraws the app's approval everywhere it was given.
Computer use from the terminal: copy the CLI connection again in the desktop app (its file was renamed).
Windows: messages that mention a local file send again.
Library: opening an item and going back works again (the page no longer gets stuck).
A chat saved with a model that is no longer available switches to the default OmniRush model and says so, instead of leaving Send disabled.
The Mac app starts again: 3.6.7 and 3.6.9 stopped with "The bundled engine was changed".

improved: Computer use: no approval on each step; one Allow per app per chat. In Normal mode it still asks before paying or buying and before typing a password.
fixed: Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the app's own keys.
Security: approvals, permission mode, project settings, plugins, MCP servers and keys can only be changed from the app's own window, not with a key read from disk.

new: What's new: see what changed in each release from the sidebar, the Help menu or the command palette, and a short note after each update.

Themes: eight presets with light and dark versions, and your own theme in Settings › Appearance with a live preview and contrast checks. Share it as a code or a file; the editor, terminal and chat all follow it.

Computer use: the agent can operate an app window you approve (screenshots, clicks, typing), with a stop control and approvals that follow your permission mode. Off until it is enabled for your account.

Editor: search, problems and language features, a split editor, editor settings, Markdown and image preview, and a Git change gutter. Format on save asks once before running a project's own formatter.
improved: Fewer repeated failed edits: when an edit can't find its text, the agent now sees the file's current lines.
The reasoning effort shown in the model picker is always the one used.
The session quality status now sits inside its chip instead of above the chat.
Only OmniRush models are offered. Other providers, and your own opencode plugins and custom tools, stay off.
fixed: Security: a project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running.
Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters.
MCP servers get the display, browser, Git, Volta and package settings they need again, while the app's own tokens stay hidden from them.
Security: Git hooks run by the editor's git panel and by parallel tasks no longer receive the app's sign-in tokens.
Security: MCP servers no longer receive the app's own sign-in tokens.
Security: the folder access check no longer reads settings or an environment file from the shared temporary folder.

new: Chat and IDE layouts: switch with the toggle at the top left or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Y. IDE puts files, changes and Git on the left, the editor and terminal in the middle and the chat on the right.
Permission modes: Careful asks before every change and command, Normal asks only before risky actions, Auto never asks. Pick one in the composer or in Settings.
Answer approvals from the keyboard: Y allows once, A for this chat, N denies.
Notifications when a task finishes or needs your approval while the window is in the background.
The Figma MCP server can be used with the key from your own environment; in Normal mode only its read tools run without asking.
improved: The chat works better when narrow: header actions fold into a menu, approval buttons wrap and the quality check stays readable.
A calmer start screen: the composer and starter prompts come first, with recent chats and search in one line underneath.
fixed: Undo keeps files you saved in the editor and refreshes open files; one undo takes back a whole turn, also after a compaction.
Skills you added are kept across updates, and skills lost in earlier updates are found again.
The question about wrapping up a chat is asked once instead of coming back.
Code from a project's own settings (plugins, tools, formatter and language-server commands) no longer runs on its own.
Chats are never sent to a sharing service.
The approval buttons fit in a narrow chat.

new: A code editor beside the chat.
Review your changes and fix what the review found. Undo the last turn while keeping your own later edits, and redo it.
Parallel tasks, each in its own copy of the project.
A home screen with recent projects and chats, and a search of past chats.
improved: The agent checks its own changes with the project's checks, keeps project notes in AGENTS.md, sees code diagnostics after edits, and writes fuller summaries when a long chat is compacted. Each can be switched off in Settings.
fixed: MCP servers from a project's own settings no longer start on their own. Only supported servers start, at a supported version, inside the project; the others are listed with the reason.

new: Send feedback from the sidebar, the Help menu or the command palette.
Web search for the model, when it is available for your account. Searches and their sources show in the chat.
improved: The unused web search setting is gone.
fixed: A chat stops before the first prompt when the project folder can't be written to, says how to fix it, and offers to choose another folder.
Limit and policy messages are shown once and are not sent again automatically.

improved: Groundwork for future features.
Usage analytics go to OmniRush's own analytics and are linked to your account. The Privacy Policy explains what is sent.
Groundwork for future features.

fixed: The sandbox reconnects on its own after it stops while the app is open, for example after a long idle time.
Large dependency installs no longer fail a turn in the sandbox.
Tool calls are closed properly when you stop a run or quit.
Security fixes for links, deep links and the developer tools port.

improved: The app repairs its local store on start when it was left damaged.
fixed: Esc stops an automatic compaction straight away.

new: When the app cannot start, it explains why and offers a reset.

improved: Reliability improvements.

new: Long chats are compacted automatically, so they stay fast.

improved: Windows: faster, more reliable start.

new: Frontier Buildathon card and an updates feed in the app.
